intro: College physics teachers explain hard ideas clearly and solve complex problems, skills used across research science. The closest of the 25 careers below is Astronomers, with a 78% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $128,820, which is 28% more than the $100,310 physics teachers in higher education earn.
why_it_works: Teaching physics means building intuition, designing labs and grading problem sets that reveal how students think. O*NET rates instructing at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, judgment at 3.75 and complex problem solving at 3.62. Astronomy, physics research and mathematics use the same depth. Every match needs no more education than you have. The gaps are programming and quality checks.
tips: Physicists earn $172,250, which is 72% more, and are a 76% match.
Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, or 47% more, and apply physics to cancer treatment.
Strengthen programming; it is the most common gap for research and industry roles.

faq.q: What jobs can former physics professors do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Astronomers (78%), Physicists (76%) and Mathematicians (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Biochemists and biophysicists are 74% matched and earn $127,410, which is 27% more than the $100,310 median for postsecondary physics teachers, though most of these roles focus on research rather than teaching.

faq.q: Which careers for physics professors pay more?
faq.a: 11 of the 25 matches pay more. Nurse Anesthetists earn $236,590 (136% more), Physicists $172,250 (72% more) and Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (47% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nurse anesthesia requires nursing training, so it is a long switch.

faq.q: Do physics professors need another degree?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than physics teachers in higher education already have, including all of the top 10. A doctoral degree is common, held by 65% of workers in the closest match, so your training covers most research roles.

faq.q: What skills should physics professors learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are programming, complex problem solving, operations monitoring and quality control analysis. Time management already rates 3.25 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so coding and applied lab skills are the main steps toward industry.
